findings_and_relationships.first_contract: If held camera aim is meant to select another downed roll sector, individually admitted tuning values must preserve a reachable switching threshold or explicitly represent an intentional disabled mode.
findings_and_relationships.trace: SignedHalfTurns permits any finite sign; state transition config uses it for width and stickiness. Its validator checks only dive handoff order. The displayed full parent validator calls this child and does not directly bound these two fields. Current server passes held aim to the current state kernel and the kernel reads installed runtime state-transition tuning.
findings_and_relationships.symbolic_case: For otherwise acceptable config, take width=1.1 and stickiness=0.0, a prone body, no existing downed roll, held aim and a finite camera target +0.5 half-turn. initial=committed=0; target difference is 0.5 and the strict >1.1 test fails; target remains prone, next=0 and lateral motion is rest. The committed 0.25+0.055555556 threshold is below 0.5, for which the helper selects RollRight. A fresh or existing committed sector has nearest-equivalent camera difference bounded near one half-turn, so a threshold above 1 can prevent a switch on the represented bounded camera path.
findings_and_relationships.limitations: This is a conditional source trace, not an executed configuration, deserialization, player, camera or runtime. Other validation or policy/entry-point constraints not read may limit supported alternate values. Setting such a width may deliberately disable switching; decide policy before assigning severity or demanding a fix. A single camera-target hypothetical does not prove a persistent live fault.
findings_and_relationships.relationships: Related 059 Q-L12-9c0f42671d4d966b6fd9 mentions dynamic tuning and native consumers but first questions the large-coordinate lattice; not automatically identical to this ordinary-sized threshold candidate. thirteen_lens_dispositions.bounded_assessment: SignedHalfTurns admits all finite signed f32, including large unwrapped coordinates; DownedFacingState custom wire conversion sanitizes nonfinite coordinates and clamps or clears lateral motion, while ordinary scalar TryFrom rejects invalid values. PositiveAnimationDuration requires a checked nonzero elapsed but not a substantive minimum. Do not declare all inputs corrupt or all normalizations obsolete.

Current tuning stores sector width and edge stickiness separately as signed finite half-turn values, and their sum controls reachability of switching sectors; independent finite admission does not enforce a useful aggregate threshold. See conditional sector-policy candidate; whether disabling switching is supported remains open.

The exact P16, a120 per-file base, 6533 pr-working, 039 catalog and 95e blobs match for both files. Preserve aim hold/release, wrap, finite scalar and wire sanitation behavior except where the final authorized policy changes it. File equality does not prove dirty whole-snapshot cleanliness.
TryFrom/serde and private policy/state fields encode meaningful distinction between checked scalar construction and source-specific wire sanitation; do not remove them simply to reduce code.

TurnPolicy keeps speed, half-turn duration and deadline operands in distinct variants; DownedFacingAim distinguishes held and released and DownedFacingPose names four sectors. Target sector and interpolated coordinate are different facts, not duplicate enum payloads by themselves.

SignedHalfTurns owns an intentionally unwrapped coordinate, distinct from nonnegative frame step, signed motion fraction, yaw and duration. It is weaker than the range semantics needed for sector width/stickiness; stronger tuning ownership may be needed without globally narrowing unwrapped roll.

The turn kernel can overflow a positive tiny quotient, and IEEE NaN multiplied by zero interacts with f32 min/max as already assessed. Finite large unwrapped coordinates can saturate the sector cast, while next coordinate is checked before retaining; their separate failures remain distinct.

The 1e-5 turn/roll and 1e-4 contact thresholds have distinct tie/deadband roles and may be tuning or numerical policy. Viewer uses 1/84 per-frame for its downed scenario, while server computes elapsed/get-up duration; intended fixture comparability and rate policy remain open.

Scoped source uses typed variants and structured animation errors; unreachable messages correspond to guarded state or mathematically bounded remainder. No magic-string identity defect established within these bodies.

Server facing carries configured get-up duration to per-frame roll and separately obtains camera target; animation tuning comes from installed cached runtime snapshot. Viewer supplies an authored fixed step. Full server/client config installation, scheduling and cross-process agreement remain open.

No duplicate canonical angle owner follows from target pose and unwrapped interpolation coordinate; they play distinct roles. Configured runtime sector threshold and viewer fixed step are potential distinct policy authorities whose intended relationship requires review.

Unwrapped signed turns, nonnegative step, bounded signed motion, sector threshold, duration, angle and final quaternion are distinct concepts. Any future threshold strengthening must not erase legitimate unwrapped state or measured zero elapsed.

Config owns authored sector policy; turn and downed-state methods own scalar and state updates; server posture projection and viewer own different input/consumer boundaries. Cross-lens ledger, canonical repair and exact aliases remain central.
